question: TO-DB-b-3 amendment 1: the count of (account, period) pairs where a landed vendor response's period lies inside DB-b-1's gold history. A fresh Black Diamond pull is admitted ONLY if this is below 5.
verdict: NO PULL. 5 is not below 5, so the landed responses carry the tie-out and no vendor egress is made.
the_correction_that_changed_the_answer: A FIRST PASS KEYED ON THE REQUESTED startDate AND GOT 4, WHICH WOULD HAVE TRIGGERED A VENDOR CALL. The order states the behaviour that makes that wrong: 'BD returns its own period list and ignores a start it does not hold.' Three rows on 0027265115 requested 2026-01-01, 2025-08-28 and 2026-03-16 against the same end and all returned the IDENTICAL -0.057098708 with daysHeld 116 -- one period under three requested starts. Keying on the requested start both (a) counts clipped duplicates as distinct, which AC1 calls a defect, and (b) discards 0076459710's rows whose EFFECTIVE start is inside the gold. The key is the EFFECTIVE period: max(requested start, the level's own startDate), cross-checked against daysHeld.
skipped_with_reason: 5,314 landed responses belong to 49F relationships that carry no roster row; the refusal clause says say so and skip, denominator printed.

Two roster accounts (0035940058 Bump, 0091939812 Macy) carry NO bd_internal_id at all -- status pending_resolution, not in dim_account_xref -- so no vendor response can be mapped to them and they cannot enter the tie-out.
Four calendar-year ranges (2024, 2025) carry daysHeld 0 and an empty timeWeightedReturns: the accounts did not exist. Skipped as vendor-absent, not as zero.
independent_corroboration: BD's own level startDate equals this seat's measured gold inception on BOTH mapped accounts: 0027265115 -> 2026-03-16 and 0076459710 -> 2026-07-08. Those dates were measured from the custodian's balance partitions by first_data_dates() before any vendor file was read, so two unrelated instruments agree.
